_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the objectives a stage is principally associated with; coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms.

_items_source.document: AQA A-level Psychology (7182) specification: 4.1 Introductory Topics in Psychology (4.1.1 Social Influence, 4.1.2 Memory, 4.1.3 Attachment, 4.1.4 Psychopathology); 4.2 Psychology in Context (4.2.1 Approaches in Psychology, 4.2.2 Biopsychology, 4.2.3 Research Methods); 4.3 Issues and Options in Psychology (4.3.1 Issues and Debates in Psychology, plus the selected options 4.3.2 Relationships, 4.3.5 Schizophrenia and 4.3.8 Aggression)
_items_source.version: The current specification (first teaching from September 2015, unchanged in core structure since), linked from aqa.org.uk/subjects/psychology/a-level/psychology-7182 and cross-checked against the original AQA-7181-7182-SP-2015.PDF specification document, itemised 2026-09-27
_items_source.numbering: AQA numbers this specification's subject content in three levels (e.g. 4.1.1 Social Influence, 4.2.3 Research Methods, 4.3.5 Schizophrenia). This course keeps its own short sequential topic.subtopic codes (SI1-9 Social Influence, MEM1-7 Memory, ATT1-10 Attachment, PSY1-4 Psychopathology; APP1-6 Approaches, BIO1-7 Biopsychology, RM1-11 Research Methods; ID1-5 Issues and Debates, REL1-5 Relationships, SCZ1-4 Schizophrenia, AGG1-3 Aggression), cross-referenced in each stage's `topic_area` to AQA's own 4.1.1-4.3.8 section numbers. The six option topics not selected for this course (Gender, Cognition and Development, Eating Behaviour, Stress, Forensic Psychology, Addiction) are itemised at a coarser grain (4-5 bullets each, coded GEN/COG/EAT/STR/FOR/ADD) purely to record them as declared exclusions; they are not taught.

_syllabus_items.title: Types and explanations of conformity (internalisation, identification, compliance; ISI/NSI)
Variables affecting conformity (Asch) and conformity to social roles (Zimbardo)
Zimbardo's Stanford Prison Experiment
Milgram's research and the situational variables affecting obedience (proximity, location, uniform)
Explanations for obedience: legitimacy of authority and the agentic state
The dispositional explanation for obedience: the Authoritarian Personality
Resistance to social influence: social support and locus of control
Minority influence: consistency, commitment, flexibility (Moscovici)
The role of social influence processes in social change
The multi-store model of memory (sensory register, STM, LTM; coding, capacity, duration)
The working memory model (central executive, phonological loop, visuo-spatial sketchpad, episodic buffer)
Explanations for forgetting: interference
Explanations for forgetting: retrieval failure due to absence of cues
Eyewitness testimony: misleading information (leading questions, post-event discussion)
Eyewitness testimony: the effect of anxiety
Improving the accuracy of eyewitness testimony: the cognitive interview
Caregiver-infant interactions (reciprocity, interactional synchrony) and Schaffer's stages of attachment
Multiple attachments and the role of the father
Animal studies of attachment: Lorenz (imprinting)
Animal studies of attachment: Harlow (contact comfort)
Learning theory (cupboard love) as an explanation of attachment
Bowlby's monotropic theory of attachment
Ainsworth's Strange Situation and types of attachment
Cultural variations in attachment (Van Ijzendoorn and Kroonenberg)
Bowlby's theory of maternal deprivation and the Romanian orphan studies (Rutter)
The influence of early attachment on childhood and adult relationships (Hazan and Shaver)
Definitions of abnormality: statistical infrequency, deviation from social norms, failure to function adequately, deviation from ideal mental health
Phobias: behavioural/emotional/cognitive characteristics, the two-process model, and behavioural treatments (systematic desensitisation, flooding)
Depression: characteristics, Beck's negative triad, Ellis's ABC model, and CBT
OCD: characteristics, genetic and neural explanations, and drug therapy
The origins of psychology (Wundt, introspection) and the behaviourist approach (classical and operant conditioning)

_syllabus_items.title: The nervous system: central and peripheral (somatic and autonomic) divisions
Neurons (sensory, relay, motor) and synaptic transmission
The endocrine system and the fight-or-flight response
Localisation of brain function and hemispheric lateralisation (split-brain research)
Plasticity and functional recovery of the brain after trauma
Ways of studying the brain: fMRI, EEG, ERPs, post-mortem examinations
Biological rhythms: circadian, infradian, ultradian; endogenous pacemakers and exogenous zeitgebers
Types of experiment: laboratory, field, natural, quasi
Experimental design: independent groups, repeated measures, matched pairs
Other research methods: observation, self-report, case studies, content analysis
Correlations; aims and hypotheses (directional/non-directional)
Sampling methods: random, systematic, stratified, opportunity, volunteer
Variables (IV/DV/EV/confounding, operationalisation), control (randomisation, standardisation, counterbalancing), demand characteristics/investigator effects, and pilot studies
Ethical issues in research and the BPS Code of Ethics and Conduct
Reliability (test-retest, inter-observer) and validity (face, concurrent, ecological, temporal)
Features of science, scientific report writing, peer review, and economic implications of research
Data handling: quantitative/qualitative and primary/secondary data, levels of measurement, descriptive statistics, distributions
Introduction to inferential testing: probability, significance, Type I/II errors, the sign test, and choosing/using statistical tests
Gender bias and cultural bias in psychological research
